name: VALHEN STEM Academy (George Mason University)
org: George Mason University College of Science, STEM Academy
what_you_do: Spend three days at Mason's Fairfax campus. You go to university lectures and do hands-on STEM challenges. Teams work on a research project. It is about a global STEM or sustainability challenge. You also explore STEM careers.
grades: Rising high school juniors (current 10th graders when applying)
who_can_apply: Virginia residents in a public or private high school, or home-schooled in Virginia. You need a GPA of 2.5 or higher. You cannot have attended the 2026 STEM Academy (VSA) or Leadership Academy (VLA). You cannot attend another VALHEN summer program in 2027. A recommendation is required. It should come from a teacher, counselor, coach or community leader. That person must not be related to you.
pay_detail: Free for selected students. Overnight students get two nights of dorm housing, meals and a daily snack. A limited number of day-only slots exist. You arrange your own transportation.
deadline_text: The 2027 program is tentatively July 28 to 30, 2027, with final dates confirmed in January 2027. The application opens in February 2027. No deadline is posted yet.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens in February 2027. Essays must be your own work (no AI generated or third-party essays). Contact STEM Academy Director Kerin Hilker-Balkissoon at khilkerb@gmu.edu.
notes: The camps list at Mason describes this program for ages 14 to 16 (rising sophomores and juniors). The program page itself says rising juniors, so use the program page. Competitive: students are selected. It is statewide for Virginia residents but held in Fairfax. It may also be on a Virginia-wide list.
